sections.h2: Where Richardson homeowners pay property tax
sections.html:
Richardson sits partly in Dallas County and partly in Collin County, so a tax payment goes to the county office that covers your house.

  • Dallas County Tax Office: 6820 LBJ Freeway, Dallas, TX 75240, 214-653-7811.
  • Collin County Tax Office: 900 E. Park Blvd, Ste 100, Plano, TX 75074, 972-881-3014.
  • Dallas Central Appraisal District: 2949 N. Stemmons Freeway, Dallas, 214-631-0910, for values and exemptions on Dallas County parcels.
  • Collin Central Appraisal District: 250 Eldorado Pkwy, McKinney, 469-742-9200, for the Collin County side.

The yearly rhythm is easy to follow with a dated example: tax for 2026 is billed in October 2026 and is not delinquent until February 1, 2027.

The council adopted the 2026-27 budget with the property tax rate held at $0.54218 per $100 of assessed valuation. The budget is $432,226,829 and it keeps a $160,000 exemption for seniors.

Estimated city-side costs for the typical Richardson homeowner
CostFY 2025-26FY 2026-27
Average taxable value of a homestead$411,065$424,062
Property tax, city portion$2,229$2,299
Water charges$1,171$1,231
Sewer charges$616$691
Drainage fee$74$86
Residential solid waste$332$344

The rate did not change, but a higher average taxable value lifts the city share of the bill by about $70 a year. New water and wastewater rates start October 1, and the monthly base charge on a 3/4-inch meter rises from $8 to $9.60. Water, sewer, drainage and trash fees arrive on separate city bills. The figures above cover the city only. Richardson ISD, the county and any other unit send their own charges through the county tax office.

Richardson does not offer the optional percentage homestead exemption, so nothing shows for it on the city's line of a Collin or Dallas County statement. Only school districts must grant a homestead exemption. Other units choose whether to adopt one.

The city does give a senior exemption of $160,000. Apply through the appraisal district for the county where your property lies, not at city hall. State-level breaks sit on top of that:

  • Richardson ISD, like every school district, must give the $140,000 residence homestead exemption.
  • Owners who are 65 or older, or disabled, shield $60,000 more from school tax.
  • After the first qualifying year, a homestead's appraised value can rise no more than 10 percent a year.
  • Filing closes before May 1. A buyer closing after New Year's Day may still claim for the rest of the year when the seller held no exemption.
  • A 100 percent VA rating brings a full exemption on the residence homestead.

Charges start the day after January 31. On the first of February the balance takes on six percent in penalty plus one percent in interest. The penalty then gains a point each month and reaches twelve percent in July, while interest never stops at a point a month. A unit that retains a collection attorney can add up to 20 percent.

You can spread payment: half by the end of November and half by the end of June. Homestead owners who are 65 or older or disabled can use four installments, and a late installment draws a six percent penalty. A waiver of penalty and interest is possible if the tax is paid by the 21st day after the owner learns of the delinquency and a written request goes in before day 181.

A protest has its own track. The filing deadline is May 15, or the 30th day after delivery of the notice when that comes later. While the dispute goes on, pay at least the undisputed tax before February 1. Gather recent sales of similar Richardson houses before the hearing, since your argument is only as strong as the comparisons behind it.

sections.h2: Back tax and a Richardson sale
sections.html:
A tax lien forms each January 1 and stays on the property through any sale. Expect the title company to require past-due amounts at closing, since no buyer receives clear title until they are cleared. Whoever owned on that January 1 is also still liable for the year's bill.

Utility accounts matter at the same time. Richardson's utility customer service line is 972-744-4120. The 2026-27 budget changed how residential wastewater is calculated, using only the prior year's November through February water use and leaving out the highest month. A seller who is closing should call customer service about ending the account so the final bill is settled. Customers over 65 with a 3/4-inch or 1-inch meter keep the old $8 base charge.

If a taxing unit sues and sells the house, a former homestead owner can buy it back for two years after the buyer's deed is filed, and other property for 180 days. Heirs selling an inherited Richardson house should first record the matching paperwork: a muniment of title order, an executor's deed, or an affidavit of death with a transfer on death deed.

Past-due tax rarely kills a deal. The usual path is to ask the county tax office that covers your parcel for a written payoff, give it to the title company, and let closing take it from your proceeds. The settlement sheet should then show who covers which part of the current year, since the January 1 owner stays liable for it.

If you are close to a sale date, gather the latest statement, proof of any exemption and the utility account details so nothing holds up the closing. A cash buyer can skip the lender's timeline, though the tax balance still gets cleared at the table.

Richardson counted 99,223 people in 2010 and 119,469 in 2020. The 2025 estimate of 118,542 is a 0.8 percent dip from 2020. Owners occupy 50.7 percent of homes, so the city splits almost evenly between owners and renters. A typical owned home is worth $431,400, rent runs $1,857 at the median and median household income is $98,111.

faqs.q: Which county do I pay Richardson property tax to?
faqs.a: Use the tax office of the county that holds your parcel. Part of Richardson is in Dallas County and part in Collin County, and each office has its own address and phone.

faqs.q: What is Richardson's property tax rate?
faqs.a: The 2026-27 city rate is $0.54218 per $100 of assessed valuation, unchanged from the prior budget. Richardson ISD, the county and other units add their own rates.

faqs.q: Does Richardson have a senior exemption?
faqs.a: Yes. The $160,000 senior property tax exemption continues in 2026-27. Ask the appraisal district for your county how to apply.

faqs.q: When does Richardson property tax become delinquent?
faqs.a: February 1 of the year after the tax year. Tax for 2026, for example, is billed in October 2026 and delinquent on February 1, 2027.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Richardson house that has back taxes?
faqs.a: Yes. Past-due tax is usually taken out of the proceeds at closing so the buyer gets clear title. Because the January 1 owner remains liable, the settlement sheet should spell out who covers which part of the year.
